discussion_comments.comment_body: Why were we able to pass the tests without this flush before?

The tests succeed due to luck. They won't be successful every time. I've tested this numerous times and the results are inconsistent. You can confirm this by checking the GitHub Actions history. https://github.com/apache/apisix/actions/runs/19564429993/job/56023083356 https://github.com/apache/apisix/actions/runs/19129422988/job/54666333550

I updated the unit tests, but this approach doesn't work for some of them because they rely on the state set by previous tests. For example
https://github.com/apache/apisix/blob/c0c906eb4d62886ffa4b0938b017dc4810cfe639/t/plugin/limit-count-redis-cluster.t#L124-L188
In these tests, test 5 expects `[200, 503, 503]` because test 4 consumed one quota, and the request limit is 2.
In my opinion, the best approach is to update these tests so that they can run independently.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
This value still contains hyphens, so it's rejected for the same reason as TEST 24/25 — the case-normalization branch (invalid as-is, valid after `string_lower`) is never exercised. To test what the title says, send a 32-char uppercase hex value like `550E8400E29B41D4A716446655440000` and assert the exported traceId is exactly the lowercased form.

Relatedly, none of the new tests cover the happy path: a valid 32-hex header being used verbatim as the traceId (TEST 16 sends one but only greps the URL). One test that sends a fixed valid value and greps for that exact traceId would pin down both the core feature and the new lowercasing behavior.
